title: Should Teenagers Spend or Save Their Allowance?
zh: 青少年的零用錢：花掉享受還是存起來？
question: Should schools teach teenagers to save money, or let them learn by spending freely?
questionZh: 學校應該教青少年存錢，還是讓他們從自由花錢中學習？
professor: We have been studying how young people learn to manage money. One survey found that teenagers spend most of their allowance on socializing, hobbies and snacks, while fewer than one in four spend anything on study materials. Some educators say this proves that schools must teach saving and financial discipline directly. Others believe teenagers should be free to spend on experiences, since that is how they learn the value of money. Which view do you agree with, and why?
david: Schools should teach saving directly. If students only learn by making mistakes, some of those mistakes, like getting into debt through buy-now-pay-later apps, could be serious. A required budgeting unit would give everyone the same basic skills before they leave school.
mary: I disagree. Spending on friends and hobbies isn't a waste; it's part of growing up. Teenagers learn to value money by running out of it once or twice. Lectures about saving rarely change anyone's habits, so schools should leave this to families and real experience.

essays.label: Essay A — Agree with David
essays.zh: 學校應直接教存錢與理財

rows.hints: I agree with David that 我同意 David 所說的 / financial literacy 理財素養 / should be taught 應該被教導 / directly 直接地
rows.sample: [[I agree with David that]] **financial literacy** [[should be taught directly]] in high school instead of being left to chance.

rows.hints: What he did not mention is that 他沒有提到的是 / unequal 不平等的 / family background 家庭背景 / guidance 指導 / fair 公平
rows.sample: [[What he did not mention is that]] learning at home is **unequal**. Some parents explain budgets and interest, while others never talk about money at all. A school course is the only **fair** way to make sure every student receives the same **guidance**.

rows.hints: When I …, I was shocked to find that 當我…時，我驚訝地發現 / spending diary 消費日記 / semester 學期 / drinks 飲料
rows.sample: [[When I]] kept a **spending diary** for a class project, [[I was shocked to find that]] I had spent more on drinks than on books in a whole **semester**. Without that assignment, I would never have noticed.

rows.hints: Mary has a point that …; however, 雖然 Mary 說…有道理，然而 / lecture 說教 / practical 實用的 / activity 活動 / change habits 改變習慣
rows.sample: [[Mary has a point that]] **lectures** rarely work; [[however,]] a good course is **practical**, not preachy. Activities like budgeting challenges actually **change habits**. When students track their own spending, they see the problem for themselves.

rows.hints: All things considered, 總而言之 / prepare … for 為…做準備 / adult life 成年生活
rows.sample: [[All things considered,]] a school finance course [[prepares]] teenagers [[for]] **adult life** better than trial and error.

essays.label: Essay B — Agree with Mary
essays.zh: 讓青少年從花錢經驗中學習

rows.hints: I share Mary's view that 我和 Mary 看法相同 / first-hand experience 親身經驗 / effective 有效的
rows.sample: [[I share Mary's view that]] teenagers learn about money most **effectively** through **first-hand experience**.

rows.hints: I would also add that 我還想補充 / spending on friends 花在朋友身上 / investment 投資 / support network 支持網絡 / mental health 心理健康
rows.sample: [[I would also add that]] spending on friends is not always a waste; it can be an **investment** in a **support network**. Shared meals and trips help students cope with exam stress, which protects their **mental health**.

rows.hints: Personally, I learned this when 我個人是在…時學到的 / run out of money 錢花光 / course 課程 / afford 負擔得起 / since then 從那時起
rows.sample: [[Personally, I learned this when]] I **ran out of money** and could not **afford** a coding course I really wanted. [[Since then,]] I have saved ten percent of my allowance every month, and no teacher had to tell me. The disappointment taught me more than any lecture.

rows.hints: David worries that …, but 雖然 David 擔心…，但 / debt 債務 / small mistake 小錯誤 / low-risk 低風險的 / pocket money 零用錢
rows.sample: [[David worries that]] mistakes could lead to **debt**, [[but]] **pocket money** is a **low-risk** place to make them. A small mistake at sixteen prevents a big one at twenty-five. Learning early is much cheaper than learning late.

rows.hints: In the end, 最終 / freedom 自由 / responsibility 責任 / go hand in hand 相輔相成
rows.sample: [[In the end,]] **freedom** and **responsibility** [[go hand in hand,]] so teenagers should be trusted to learn by spending.
